description: Orchestrates Active Directory object migration from AWS Simple AD to AWS Managed Microsoft AD (users, OUs, groups + memberships) via csvde export and AD cmdlet import. NOTE 1: Simple AD cannot preserve passwords (no trust, Samba 4, so ADMT/PES is not supported); migrated users receive a reset password and must change it at first logon. NOTE 2: The source Simple AD admin is 'Administrator'; the target Managed AD admin is 'Admin'. The Managed AD Admin account cannot write to the domain root (AWS-owned), so all objects are recreated under the directory's NetBIOS OU (OU=<ShortName>,<domainDN>), resolved automatically from the directory. The source 'Administrator' account is excluded and never recreated. NOTE 3: Credentials are read from a single AWS Secrets Manager secret (migrationSecretId) holding JSON {"source":{"username","password"},"target":{"username","password"}}. The target block is required; the source block is OPTIONAL. If a source username+password is present the export binds to the source Simple AD with those credentials through the LDAP bind API (an authenticated LdapConnection, AuthType=Negotiate), so the password is never placed on a process command line; if absent, the export binds as the Run Command execution identity on the domain-joined management box (the originally tested path). The automation/instance role needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret (plus kms:Decrypt only if a customer-managed KMS key is used).

sourceADServer.description: (Required) IP address or DNS name of the source Simple AD server.

migrationSecretId.description: (Required) Name or ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret holding migration credentials as JSON: {"source":{"username":"Administrator","password":"..."},"target":{"username":"Admin","password":"..."}}. The 'target' block is REQUIRED (used to bind to Managed AD on import). The 'source' block is OPTIONAL; when present its username+password are used to bind to the source Simple AD through the LDAP bind API (never placed on a process command line), otherwise the export binds as the Run Command execution identity. Create the secret out-of-band so no password is ever passed as an automation input.

managedADId.description: (Required) Directory ID of the target Managed AD (d-xxxxxxxxxx). Used to resolve the target DC IP via ds:DescribeDirectories.

useSourceBind.description: (Optional) If 'true', the source export binds to the source Simple AD using the secret's source.username/source.password. The bind is performed through the LDAP bind API (an authenticated LdapConnection with AuthType=Negotiate), so the password is passed in the authentication call and never appears on a process command line. Use this ONLY when the management box is NOT joined to the source domain. Default 'false' = bind as the Run Command execution identity (the tested path when the box is joined to the source domain). The secret may contain a source block without this being set; the explicit source-credential bind is applied ONLY when useSourceBind=true AND the source creds are present.

instanceId.description: (Required) EC2 instance ID of the domain-reachable management box (with RSAT-AD / csvde) where migration scripts run.

AutomationAssumeRole.description: (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Systems Manager Automation to perform actions on your behalf. Must allow secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on migrationSecretId, ssm:PutParameter/GetParameter on the /ad-migration/* params, ssm:SendCommand/GetCommandInvocation to the instance, and ds:DescribeDirectories on the target (plus kms:Decrypt only if the secret uses a customer-managed KMS key). The management EC2 instance role also needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue since the scripts read the secret on-box via Run Command. Leave empty to run as the invoking identity.

mainSteps.name: Preflight
mainSteps.description: Validate the management box can run the migration: AD module present, csvde present, source + target DCs reachable, and the Secrets Manager migration secret is readable and well-formed (target creds present).

commands: if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name ActiveDirectory)) { throw 'ActiveDirectory module not found. Install RSAT-AD-PowerShell.' }
foreach ($t in @('csvde.exe')) { if (-not (Get-Command $t -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw "$t not found on PATH" } }
if (-not (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName $src -Port 389 -InformationLevel Quiet)) { throw "Cannot reach source DC $src on LDAP/389" }
Write-Host 'Reading migration secret from Secrets Manager...' -ForegroundColor Cyan
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($secRaw)) { throw 'Migration secret SecretString is empty' }
try { $sec = $secRaw | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { throw 'Migration secret is not valid JSON' }

if (-not $sec.target -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($sec.target.username) -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($sec.target.password)) { throw 'Migration secret must contain target.username and target.password' }
if ($sec.source -and $sec.source.username -and -not $sec.source.password) { throw 'Migration secret source.username present but source.password missing' }
$srcMode = if ($sec.source -and $sec.source.username -and $sec.source.password) { 'explicit LDAP bind (source creds)' } else { 'Run Command identity' }
Write-Host "Secret OK. Source bind mode: $srcMode" -ForegroundColor Yellow

mainSteps.name: ResolveTargetDCAndSetParameters
mainSteps.description: Resolve the target Managed AD DC IP from the directory ID (ds:DescribeDirectories -> DnsIpAddrs) and persist the non-secret migration parameters to SSM Parameter Store. The password is NOT written here; it is read from the pre-created SecureString param.

commands: Write-Host 'Resolving target Managed AD DC IP...' -ForegroundColor Cyan
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($targetDcIp)) { throw 'Could not resolve target DC IP from DescribeDirectories DnsIpAddrs' }

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($shortName)) { throw 'Could not resolve target NetBIOS ShortName from DescribeDirectories. In Managed AD all objects MUST be created under OU=<ShortName>,<domainDN>; the domain root is AWS-owned and not writable.' }
Write-Host "Target DC IP: $targetDcIp | NetBIOS OU: $shortName" -ForegroundColor Yellow

mainSteps.name: RunExportScript
mainSteps.description: Export OUs, users, groups and group memberships from the source Simple AD using csvde over LDAP. Simple AD is Samba 4 with no Active Directory Web Services, so the AD PowerShell module cannot be used against the source; all source reads are csvde/LDAP.

commands: # Export-ViaLdap: produce the same raw CSVs csvde would, but via LdapConnection so the
# bind password goes through the logon/bind API and never appears on a process command line
# (fixes CWE-214 / finding 8131e128). Used ONLY for the useSourceBind=true path.
# Emits columns matching the csvde -l attribute lists so downstream filtering is unchanged.
# Credential via NetworkCredential -> goes through the bind API, NOT argv.
$conn.Bind()   # explicit bind; throws on bad credential
# Paged search helper: returns all entries for a filter+attrs, handling the 1000-entry page limit.
# ---- Group memberships (member is multi-valued -> ';'-joined to match csvde) ----
# (8131e128 / CWE-214) useSourceBind=true: bind via LdapConnection+NetworkCredential so the source
# admin password goes through the bind API and NEVER appears on a process command line (csvde -b
# would put it in argv -> Win 4688 / Sysmon EID1 / EDR -> SIEM). Produces the same raw CSVs.
Write-Host "Export will bind via LDAP (useSourceBind=true; credential via bind API, not argv)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
# Domain-joined box, no explicit creds: csvde binds as the Run Command execution identity (no -b,
# so no password anywhere). Original tested path.
Write-Host "Export will bind as the Run Command execution identity (no -b, useSourceBind=$useSourceBind)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
# ---- Exclusion helpers (verified against real Simple AD contents) ----
# csvde LDAP negative-wildcard DN matching does NOT reliably exclude CN=Builtin, so we export
# broadly (incl. isCriticalSystemObject) and filter in PowerShell by three rules:
#  (c) AWS/Simple-AD service objects (AWS_* / AWS Delegated *, krbtgt, Guest, Administrator).
# Well-known DEFAULT groups that live in CN=Users (not CN=Builtin) and that Simple AD/Samba does
# NOT flag with isCriticalSystemObject, so they must be denied by name. Verified against live export.

$wellKnownGroupDeny = @('Domain Admins','Domain Users','Domain Guests','Domain Computers','Domain Controllers','Enterprise Admins','Schema Admins','Cert Publishers','DnsAdmins','DnsUpdateProxy','Group Policy Creator Owners','RAS and IAS Servers','Allowed RODC Password Replication Group','Denied RODC Password Replication Group','Read-only Domain Controllers','Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers','Protected Users','Key Admins','Enterprise Key Admins','Cloneable Domain Controllers')
# Users: export broadly with isCriticalSystemObject, then filter.
# Groups: export broadly with isCriticalSystemObject, then filter.
# Group memberships via csvde/LDAP (Simple AD is Samba 4 with NO ADWS, so the AD PowerShell
# module / Get-ADGroup does NOT work against it - confirmed. csvde over LDAP does.)
# Export every group's 'member' attribute broadly, then keep only (group,member) pairs where
# BOTH the group and the member survived the user/group filtering above. This automatically
# drops built-in groups, foreign-security-principals, and privileged default groups.
# Build DN -> sAMAccountName lookup from the FILTERED user and group exports only.
# Only process groups that survived filtering (i.e. are in the migrated set).
# csvde emits multi-valued 'member' as a single ';'-separated field.
Write-Host "Members skipped (not in migrated set): $skippedMembers" -ForegroundColor Yellow
# (#6) On SUCCESS, remove the intermediate *-raw.csv files (full raw PII) that the import step
# never consumes; the filtered users.csv/groups.csv/memberships.csv remain for the import step.
foreach ($raw in @('users-raw.csv','groups-raw.csv','group-members-raw.csv')) { $rp = Join-Path $exportPath $raw; if (Test-Path $rp) { Remove-Item -Path $rp -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } }
# (#6) export failure scrub: if the export throws partway, the import step never runs and its
# finally-cleanup never fires, so PII CSVs would linger on the box. Remove them here, then rethrow.

mainSteps.name: RunImportScript
mainSteps.description: Import OUs, users, groups and group memberships into the target Managed AD. Users are created with a per-user random password (meets Managed AD complexity) and ChangePasswordAtLogon.

commands: # Read target bind credentials from Secrets Manager (target block is required; validated in Preflight).
$migMarker = 'ADWSMigrated'  # (#9) stamp on created objects so re-runs recognise our own objects
# DN builders handle ANY number of domain labels
# Managed AD: the domain root is AWS-owned and NOT writable by the Admin account.
# Every migrated object MUST be created under the directory's NetBIOS OU: OU=<ShortName>,<domainDN>.
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($netbiosOU)) { throw 'target-netbios-ou SSM param is empty; cannot safely place objects (domain root is not writable in Managed AD).' }
# Convert a source DN to the target. Objects under a real OU keep their sub-path under the NetBIOS OU.
# Objects in default containers (CN=Users / CN=Computers) have no equivalent writable container under the
# NetBIOS OU, so they are remapped directly into the NetBIOS OU (flattened).

function New-RandomPassword { $lower=97..122; $upper=65..90; $digit=48..57; $special=@(33,35,37,42,64); $all=$lower+$upper+$digit+$special; $rng=[System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::Create(); function Pick($set){ $b=[byte[]]::new(4); $rng.GetBytes($b); $n=[System.BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b,0); [char]$set[[int]($n % [uint32]$set.Count)] } $chars=@(); $chars+=Pick $lower; $chars+=Pick $upper; $chars+=Pick $digit; $chars+=Pick $special; for($i=$chars.Count; $i -lt 20; $i++){ $chars+=Pick $all } for($i=$chars.Count-1; $i -gt 0; $i--){ $b=[byte[]]::new(4); $rng.GetBytes($b); $j=[int]([System.BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b,0) % [uint32]($i+1)); $t=$chars[$i]; $chars[$i]=$chars[$j]; $chars[$j]=$t } $rng.Dispose(); -join $chars }
# NOTE: user identifiers (sAMAccountName, UPN, names) are PII. SSM Run Command output is retained
# in cleartext for 30 days, so we emit COUNTS to the console, not per-user identifiers.
# Preserve the source account enabled/disabled state. userAccountControl is a bitmask;
# bit 0x2 (ACCOUNTDISABLE) means the source account was DISABLED. Use a bitwise test, not
# equality, because the field is cumulative (e.g. 514 = 512 NORMAL + 2 DISABLE).
# (#9) object already exists: if WE created it on a prior run (carries $migMarker), treat it
# as ours so memberships can complete on re-run. Otherwise it is an unrelated collision (skip).
# Privileged/well-known target group names we must never merge migrated members into, even if a
# same-named group already exists in the target (name-collision privilege-escalation guard, #7).

$privGroupDeny = @("domain admins","enterprise admins","schema admins","administrators","account operators","server operators","backup operators","print operators","group policy creator owners","dnsadmins","key admins","enterprise key admins","protected users","aws delegated administrators","aws delegated domain name system administrators")
# (#9) same marker check for groups so a re-run can add memberships to groups WE created earlier.
# Runs after users AND groups exist. Resolves each member by sAMAccountName in the target,
# so it is correct regardless of which OU the member landed in and handles nested groups
# (the member group was created in the Groups pass above).
# (#7) Only add members to groups THIS run created. If a same-named group already existed in the
# target it may be a different, possibly privileged, group; merging migrated members into it could
# escalate privilege. Skip those, and hard-deny well-known privileged names as defense in depth.
# (#2) Only add a member that THIS run created. If the member name matches a DIFFERENT
# pre-existing target account (the source user was skipped as a name-collision on import),
# adding it would attach the WRONG person to the migrated group. Mirror the group guard.
# (#2) Fail the step if ANY per-item error occurred during import. Previously these counts were
# written to host but the step still reported Success, silently swallowing partial failures.

if ($totalImportErrors -gt 0) { throw "Import completed with $totalImportErrors error(s): OUs=$ouError Users=$uError Groups=$gError Memberships=$mError. See step log for per-item messages (identifiers suppressed)." }
# (fae0bb03) Systemic-failure guard: even if the per-item counters were ever lost in a refactor,
# a run that exported users but created/skipped NONE of them is a wholesale failure (e.g. target
# write permission denied on OU=$netbiosOU, or the target DC became unreachable after preflight).
# Fail closed so MigrationComplete / the WorkSpaces document do not proceed against an empty directory.

if ($exportedUserCount -gt 0 -and $uCreated -eq 0 -and $uSkipped -eq 0) { throw "No users were created or skipped from $exportedUserCount exported row(s). The import did nothing - check the target credential's write permission on OU=$netbiosOU and target DC reachability, then re-run." }
# (#10) Always remove the exported CSVs (they contain user PII) even if the import threw,
# so no identity data is left on the management box after a failed or partial run.

mainSteps.name: MigrationComplete
mainSteps.description: AD object migration complete. Proceed to WorkSpaces recreate (WorkSpaces-Recreate-Orchestrator) once the directory has replicated.
